ai.description: This small snake reaches 30–40 cm. It is characterized by a dark brown dorsum with a distinct, vivid orange vertebral stripe and a white venter. A dark collar marks the nape.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Oligodon erythrorhachis* is uniquely distinguished by a vivid, continuous orange-red vertebral stripe running down the center of its otherwise dark, uniform dorsal scales.
ai.habitat: The Namsang Kukri snake inhabits the dense, humid tropical evergreen forests of Northeast India, typically found at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Namsang Kukri snake is primarily nocturnal and utilizes its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice through reptile eggs, which form a significant part of its diet.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon erythrorhachis* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs. While specific breeding data is limited, it likely reproduces during the pre-monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Oligodon erythrorhachis* is endemic to Northeast India, specifically recorded in the states of Arunachal Pradesh and Assam within the Eastern Himalayan foothills.
